🐇 Jackalope (Bad Eden)

“You don’t spot a Jackalope.
You notice the world flinch, and then realize why.”

Jackalopes are the children of Bad Eden’s worst habits: speed as survival, superstition as armor, and motion as a moral stance. Half remembered from pre-Shattering folklore and half assembled by radiation, rumor, and bad luck, Jackalopes exist in the narrow margin between escape and impact.

They are fast because they have to be. They are twitchy because the world has trained them that stillness is how you die.

In the wastes, Jackalopes are blamed for everything: sudden storms, misfiring guns, caravans that vanish without a sound. None of this is quite fair. Jackalopes don’t cause disaster — they just arrive early enough to leave before it happens.

Survivors, Not Heroes

Jackalopes are not built for long stands or glorious last moments. They live by refusing to be where the violence finishes. When a fight breaks out, a Jackalope has already mapped three exits, ranked them by risk, and is quietly irritated that you haven’t.

Their horns are not trophies. They are warnings. The old saying in Bad Eden goes:

“If a Jackalope lowers its head, something has already gone wrong.”

Bad Omen Runners

Where Jackalopes settle, paths form. Trails twist. Routes that used to be safe become “unlucky,” while dangerous crossings start to feel… navigable. Factions that listen to their Jackalopes survive longer. Factions that ignore them tend to discover what was following the Jackalope in the first place.

In strategic play, Jackalopes don’t dominate territory — they shape movement. They scout, misdirect, and quietly reduce the cost of staying alive just long enough to matter.

In Bad Eden

Jackalopes thrive in irradiated scrublands, half-collapsed transit corridors, and the uncomfortable edge between two factions who don’t trust each other yet. They are rarely leaders, but they are almost always present just before a situation becomes irreversible.

If you see Jackalope tracks circling your hex, you are not under attack.

But you are being advised.
